1: # SmolLM3 and Phi-4-mini on openTPU
2: 
3: openTPU runs two Llama-style decoders of 3-4B parameters:
4: [SmolLM3-3B](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B) and
5: [Phi-4-mini-instruct](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct). They are Qwen3
6: without the RMSNorm on each q and k head, so they run on Qwen3's code (`opentpu/llm/qwen3.py`):
7: its DRAM image, kernels, resident decode and chunked prefill. `opentpu/llm/llama.py` only reads
8: their configs. The ISA, the RTL, the bitstream and the W8A8 numerics are the same as for the
9: other models.

21: ## The models
22: 
23: - **SmolLM3-3B**: 36 layers, hidden size 2048, 16 query heads and 4 KV heads of 128, a SwiGLU
24:   MLP 11008 wide, a 128,256-token vocabulary and a tied LM head. RoPE (theta 5e6) runs in 27
25:   layers; every fourth layer (3, 7, ..., 35) has no positional encoding ("NoPE",
26:   `no_rope_layers`).
27: - **Phi-4-mini-instruct** (3.8B): 32 layers, hidden size 3072, 24 query heads and 8 KV heads of
28:   128, a SwiGLU MLP 8192 wide, a 200,064-token vocabulary and a tied LM head. The checkpoint
29:   fuses q, k and v into `qkv_proj` and gate and up into `gate_up_proj`. RoPE covers the first 96
30:   of each head's 128 dimensions (`partial_rotary_factor` 0.75, theta 1e4) and is LongRoPE: up to
31:   `original_max_position_embeddings` (4096) positions Hugging Face uses the short factors, which
32:   divide the frequencies (all 1.0 in this checkpoint), and scales cos and sin by the attention
33:   factor `sqrt(1 + ln(131072 / 4096) / ln(4096))` = 1.1902.
34: 
35: Both have no biases and plain RMSNorm, and neither uses a sliding window.

66: **The embedding is gathered from the int8 LM head.** An fp32 embedding table would be 1.0 GB
67: (SmolLM3) or 2.3 GB (Phi-4-mini): beside int8 weights it does not fit the card's 4 GiB. The tied
68: LM head is already in DRAM as int8 with one scale per 128-block, so the device reads the token's
69: row out of it with the shared table gather (`kernels/gather.py`, `gather_row`): the row streams
70: as rows of one block each against a one-hot operand (row j of one-hot block k is 1 at element
71: 4k + j at MCOLS 4), so each MM gives four elements of every block, dequantized by the MXU's own
72: arithmetic, `f32(f32(i2f(127 q) * s) * f32(1/127))`, within an ulp of `q * s`; one copy per
73: block puts the row in order. The one-hot operand sits in the image's lookup tables. The resident
74: decode, the per-position programs and the prefill runs all gather their rows on the device, with
75: the token ids as run arguments or compiled into the program, so the host never dequantizes a row
76: (`Engine.device_inputs`, [host.md](host.md)). `qwen3.gathered_rows` (`gather.dequant_row`) is
77: the host's reference for the tests, and the float64 emulation quantizes the embedding row too.
78: With a 4-bit LM head the image holds an int8 table of its own. The gather adds 49 (SmolLM3) or
79: 57 (Phi-4-mini) instructions to the resident decode program, and a token id costs it two run
80: arguments (the row's byte offset and its scales' offset) instead of one.

82: **Weights are read lazily.** `load_weights` returns a mapping that converts each tensor to fp32
83: when it is first used (`qwen3.Weights`), so a 3-4B checkpoint (12-15 GB in fp32) is never all in
84: memory: building the image quantizes one tensor at a time.

1: # TinyStories-260K through qwen3.c and Vortex
2: 
3: The initial test uses the smallest published Karpathy TinyStories checkpoint:
4: 260K parameters, dimension 64, five transformer layers, eight query heads,

6: BOS exercise 288 matrix projections and produce 4096 logits.

8: The host is the separate [`allbilly/qwen3.c`](https://github.com/allbilly/qwen3.c)

11: distinct converted-checkpoint magic; the normal Qwen3 entry point rejects it.
12: The source FP32 checkpoint and tokenizer have pinned SHA-256 checksums.
13:

15: scales and FP32 output. Weights stay resident between tokens. Attention,
